proof.text: The Noetherian affine V makes U intersect V quasi-compact; choose a finite cover by basic opens D(f_i) inside U intersect V. Each f_i belongs to p because y lies outside U. The direct image is quasi-coherent by the qcqs pushforward theorem. Its affine module P therefore localizes on basic opens. Restriction from P to the product of the P[1/f_i] is injective by sheaf separatedness on U intersect V.

Localization is exact and commutes with finite products, so P_p injects into the product of (P[1/f_i])_p. An element killed by pR_p has zero image in each factor, since f_i lies in p and is invertible in that factor. Hence it is zero. The localized inclusion S_p into P_p is injective, so the same is true in S_p. In particular pR_p is not associated to S_p.

title: boundary localized submodule has no maximal associated prime
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $U$ an open subscheme, $N$ a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent], and $V$ an affine open. Write $R=\mathcal O_L(V)$ and $P=(j_*(N|_U))(V)$ for $j:U\hookrightarrow L$. Let $S\subseteq P$ be a finitely generated $R$-submodule [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $p$ a prime ideal of $R$. Set $y=h_V.\mathrm{fromSpec}(p)$, the corresponding point of $V$. If $y\notin U$, then the maximal ideal of R_p is not in the associated primes of S_p.

lean.statement:
theorem boundary_maximal_not_associated
    {L : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian L] (U : L.Opens) (N : L.Modules)
    (hqc : N.IsQuasicoherent) (V : L.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (S : Submodule (L.presheaf.obj (op V))
      (((Modules.pushforward U.ι).obj
        ((Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj N)).val.obj (op V)))
    (hS : S.FG) (p : Ideal (L.presheaf.obj (op V))) [p.IsPrime]
    (hy : hV.fromSpec ⟨p, inferInstance⟩ ∉ U) :
    IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (Localization.AtPrime p) ∉
      associatedPrimes (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule.AtPrime p S)
